Violet arises from and responds to the emotional torment of that period, S.’s urging Sophia
Stacey not to reveal him as author aims to conceal the poem’s origin in his acutely strained
relations with Mary. The poem that he tailored from his draft and sent to Sophia might of
course also be understood as expressing S.’s feelings for her, equally a motive for secrecy.
 Drafts in Nbk 11, in which S. entered a wide range of poems that he left incomplete, can
be difficult to date. On a Dead Violet was very probably drafted after William’s death on 7
June 1819 and certainly before Mary’s letter to Sophia Stacey of 7 March 1820 was posted to her
(perhaps a few days after 7 March: SC x 869) — though exactly when is uncertain. In BSM xviii,
pp. xxxix–xlviii, Nancy Goslee argues on the basis of MS evidence that On a Dead Violet as well
